items.title: Magnarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: There was a trumpet player from Pittsburgh also, Danny Conn. He passed away recently, but he was a great trumpet player from Pittsburgh.

ctx.x: It’s interesting, we’re in Utica, and you think well like jazz in Utica in Upstate New York, but you sort of had an aha moment in Syracuse with Sal Amico you were talking about?

Yeah, well that’s why I got really inspired to make jazz my life and my career. It was the summer of 1983 I think it was, and Sal Amico and J.R. Montrose were working in Syracuse every Wednesday, I think it was every Wednesday and Thursday. And I would sit in and play as much as I could, and I was so turned on by the music. Also Joe Romano played there and Andy Krupsky from New York came up and played. There was a trumpet player from Pittsburgh also, Danny Conn. He passed away recently, but he was a great trumpet…
When you went to see them, in your head were you thinking what the heck are those guys thinking about? How did they negotiate their way through these songs? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -1-
